newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish opposition ready to rule - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Turkish opposition ready to rule - spokesman.

text.p: Turkey's main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz is ready to take power to solve a political crisis which led Islamist Necmettin Erbakan to resign as prime minister this week, a spokesman said.

"Hope for a new start for the country has been born," Cumhur Ersumer, spokeman for Yilmaz's Motherland Party (ANAP) told a news conference. "ANAP is ready to take over the duties of the administration," he said.
President Suleyman Demirel has invited Yilmaz to his residence at 5 p.m. (1400 GMT) on Friday amid speculation the Motherland leader would be asked to head a new "Islamist-free" government.
Yilmaz, a staid conservative, is one of the favourites to be appointed by Demirel as prime minister-designate following Erbakan's resignation on Wednesday.
Yilmaz was confident he could head a government that would get past a parliamentary vote of confidence, despite having no clear majority on paper.
"There is an extremely high possibility that a government formed under me can win a vote of confidence," he told the NTV television news channel late on Thursday night.
